problem: On mobile (375px and 414px), the projects table (NAME | TYPE | RECIPES | STATUS | PRIORITY | COMPLETION | DELETE) does not reflow — it stays a horizontal-scrolling table with the COMPLETION column and DELETE link clipped off-screen. WCAG 2.2 §1.4.10 requires content to be usable at 320 CSS px wide without horizontal scrolling. Recruits using phones will swipe-discover the COMPLETION % and the delete control, costing time and confidence.
fix: At ≤768px breakpoint, swap the table for a stacked card layout per project row (name as title, type badge inline, recipe swatches inline, status pill below, completion as full-width progress bar, delete as a kebab menu). Or hide PRIORITY + COMPLETION columns on mobile and surface them inside each card on tap.

principle: NN/g Heuristic 5 (Error prevention) + Heuristic 1 (Visibility of system status)
location: /projects/[id] STAGES panel + and − buttons before OWNED > 0
screenshot: n/a (verified in live recruit session 13:04 UTC)
problem: On a brand-new project with OWNED = 0, pressing the keyboard shortcut 'b' (or clicking the + button on BUILD) silently does nothing — there is no toast, no inline message, no disabled-state cue. The reason is that BUILD cannot exceed OWNED (correct domain logic), but the empty state never reveals this rule. A recruit sees the helper text 'PRESS THE LETTER TO BUMP' and tries it — nothing happens. They will think the app is broken before they discover they need to increment OWNED first. Side effect: when they later press a downstream key like 'a' (paint), the inline error 'Paint can't exceed Prime (0).' appears — but the earlier failed b-presses got no error at all.
fix: Two changes: (a) Visually disable + buttons whose target value is currently capped (greyed-out, cursor not-allowed, aria-disabled=true) so users can't try and fail. (b) When the user presses a stage-bump key/button that is capped, surface the same red inline error ('Build can't exceed Owned (0). Add models first.') rather than failing silently — same pattern that already works for Paint/Prime.

principle: NN/g Heuristic 9 (Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors)
location: Recipe detail page → ASSIGN TO PROJECT dropdown → click target project
screenshot: n/a (verified once at 13:06 UTC, could not reproduce at 13:14 UTC)
problem: On the first attempt to assign the 'Necron Warrior Bone' recipe to the 'Necron Warriors' project via the recipe-page dropdown, the page crashed to a generic error screen: '⚠ This page couldn't load — Reload to try again, or go back.' with Reload/Back buttons. Console showed 'Error: An unexpected response was received from the server.' (Next.js server action 500). Reload recovered. The assignment was not committed (the project still showed '+ ATTACH' and no recipe on next visit). On a second attempt 8 minutes later, the same flow succeeded. The failure was transient but real and would scare recruits — and the generic error page does not tell them what to do beyond Reload / Back (no 'your work was not saved' confirmation).
fix: Two parts: (a) Investigate the underlying server action failure — likely a race or a deploy-cold-start edge in the assign mutation; add server-side telemetry to capture stack traces. (b) Replace the generic 'unexpected response' page with a softer toast-style error overlay that says 'Couldn't attach the recipe — your work wasn't saved. Try again?' with a retry button that re-fires the same action. The current full-page error loses the user's context.

location: /projects/[id] COLOR SCHEME box → click + tile (when no recipe attached) vs /projects table row + ATTACH link
problem: Two different affordances for 'attach a recipe to this project' lead to different behaviours: (a) On the leaf workspace, clicking a + tile in the COLOR SCHEME box does nothing visible until a recipe is created/attached elsewhere — the click highlights the tile but no picker opens. (b) From the /projects table, clicking '+ ATTACH' on a row creates a NEW empty recipe auto-named '<Project> scheme' and attaches it — without offering existing recipes from the user's library. A recruit who already has a recipe built in /recipes will not see a path from the leaf workspace or + ATTACH to 'pick from my library'. The mental model 'I have this recipe, now I attach it' has no UI to support it from the project side; you have to go to /recipes and use ASSIGN TO PROJECT ▼.
fix: Make + ATTACH on the project row open a modal with two options: 'Pick from your library' (list of existing recipes) and 'Start a new recipe for this project' (current behaviour). Same modal triggered when the COLOR SCHEME + tile is clicked on the leaf workspace before any recipe exists. Inverts the current implicit hierarchy so the recruit doesn't have to know about /recipes to discover that existing recipes can be reused.

principle: Refactoring UI § Hierarchy + NN/g Heuristic 8 (Aesthetic and minimalist design)
location: ColorPicker drawer (all instances — recipe edit, /tools/match target chip, /tools/gradient hex chips)
screenshot: n/a (verified on /tools/match at 13:09 UTC and /tools/gradient at 13:10 UTC)
problem: The slide-out ColorPicker drawer renders its title twice. Example on /tools/match: header bar says 'MATCH TARGET' in cyan, then immediately below in white the same string 'MATCH TARGET' appears again as an h2/h3-level title. Same on /tools/gradient where SHADOW appears twice. It reads as a render bug rather than intentional emphasis. Heuristic 8 violation (every element should earn its place).
fix: Remove the inner heading; let the drawer header bar be the only title. Or, if the inner heading is meant to label the field being edited, change it to a smaller secondary heading like 'Editing: Shadow slot' so the two strings serve distinct roles.

principle: NN/g Heuristic 1 (Visibility of system status) + NN/g Heuristic 2 (Match between system and real world)
location: /tools/gradient — click hex chip on SHADOW field opens ColorPicker drawer
problem: When you click the SHADOW hex chip on /tools/gradient to edit the shadow color, the ColorPicker drawer opens with the wheel positioned at the PREVIOUS color (#47D1D1 cyan — left over from another session) rather than initialized to the current SHADOW value (#072547). The drawer is supposed to let the recruit refine an existing color, but it visually appears to be picking from scratch. The recruit may not realize their existing color is preserved if they cancel.
fix: On drawer open, initialize wheel position, hex value, and LIGHTNESS slider to the current value of the field being edited. Same applies to BASE and HIGHLIGHT chip clicks. Verify the same fix lands on /tools/match TARGET HEX chip click.

location: /projects FOCUS panel — when a project has multiple recipes attached
screenshot: n/a (observed via /recipes table showing 2 recipes both ATTACHED TO 'Necron Warriors')
problem: A single project can have multiple recipes attached (verified by attaching two recipes — 'Necron Warriors scheme' and 'Necron Warrior Bone' — both showing 'Necron Warriors' in ATTACHED TO). But the FOCUS panel and the leaf project COLOR SCHEME box only display ONE recipe at a time (the latest-attached). There is no UI affordance to switch between attached recipes, and per-step notes the recruit wrote against the previous recipe silently 'disappear' from view when a new recipe becomes the displayed one. Notes are still persisted, but the recruit has no way to discover that.
fix: When a project has 2+ attached recipes, render a horizontal tab/segmented-control above the slot grid: '[ Necron Warrior Bone ] [ Necron Warriors scheme ]'. Default selection is the most recently used. Same control on the leaf project COLOR SCHEME box. If the project has only one recipe, no tab bar — keep current single-recipe rendering.

principle: NN/g Heuristic 2 (Match between system and real world)
location: ColorPicker drawer → LIBRARY search — picking magenta (#D1476F) returns 'Rubber Black', 'Nato Black' in the top 50 matches
screenshot: n/a (verified at 13:02 UTC during recipe slot 1 creation)
problem: The LIBRARY paint matcher in the color picker drawer returns a fixed list of 50 matches that doesn't appear to be sorted strictly by perceptual similarity to the picked color. When the user picks magenta on the wheel, top results include AK Interactive 'Pastel Pink', 'Rubber Black', 'Nato Black', 'WWI German Mauve', 'Purple', 'Deep Purple'. Pink and purples make sense, but Rubber Black and Nato Black are far from magenta — they're filler that erodes confidence in the matcher. Compare to the standalone /tools/match page which shows match scores (1.1, 2.4 etc.) sorted properly.
fix: Apply the same MATCH score sort the standalone /tools/match uses (CIE2000 ΔE or whichever metric is canonical). Show the score next to each match (e.g. '· 2.4' dim text). If the goal is breadth-of-brands, cap matches at ΔE < threshold and show 'no closer matches' rather than padding with far-off paints.

location: /sign-up form — Username and Password autocomplete attributes
screenshot: n/a (inferred from browser autocomplete behavior during recruit_r9 account creation)
problem: On /sign-up, the form likely lacks explicit autocomplete='new-password' on the password fields, because the browser pre-fills the password from a saved sign-in entry of an unrelated account ('Test1234'). Pre-filling a sign-in password into a sign-up form is technically incorrect for password managers and causes confusion (a recruit sees masked dots in PASSWORD before they've typed anything).
fix: Add autocomplete='new-password' to the PASSWORD and CONFIRM PASSWORD inputs on /sign-up, and autocomplete='username' on the USERNAME input. On /sign-in, use autocomplete='current-password' instead.

location: /library at mobile 414px — paint name column truncates aggressively
problem: At 414×896, paint names truncate after ~16 characters ('507a Admiralty…', '3b Au Basic Pro…'). With a phone-friendly viewport there's enough room to show ~25-30 chars before truncating. The brand column also truncates ('AK Interac…') even though there's whitespace right of the BRAND column.
fix: Tighten the column proportions at mobile breakpoints — give NAME 1.5× the width of BRAND, and let BRAND wrap to two lines if needed (better than ellipsizing a recognizable brand name). Alternatively, hide the BRAND column on mobile and put it as a small caption below the paint name.

problem: The top status bar shows 'NET · ON' normally but flips to 'NET · LAG' (amber) during slow server actions. This is a nice power-user signal but the visual transition between ON and LAG is abrupt — and there's no tooltip explaining what LAG means. A recruit sees an amber warning indicator on first slow request and may worry their connection is broken. Heuristic 1 says feedback should be meaningful; this needs a one-line explanation.
fix: Add a title/aria-describedby tooltip on the NET pill: 'NET LAG — the server's responding slower than usual. Your work is still saving.' Optionally, only show LAG state if the request takes >1500ms (not on every micro-spike).

location: Recipe color slots on /projects FOCUS panel — Slot 1 vs Slot 2 cyan shades
problem: When I created two slots in the 'Necron Warriors scheme' recipe by clicking different wheel positions, both rendered as slightly different cyan shades (Slot 1: bright #47D1D1, Slot 2: a darker teal) but both display as 'BASECOAT · #47D1D1' in the step row — the same hex string. The visual swatch doesn't match the labeled hex, which suggests the slot is rendering the LIGHTNESS-adjusted preview rather than the saved value. Minor visual inconsistency but it can confuse a recruit comparing what's painted vs what's saved.
fix: Ensure the slot tile background-color is computed from the same hex that the label shows. If a darker preview is intentional for visual depth, label it 'live preview' vs 'saved hex' clearly — but easier fix is to remove the preview tint and just paint the swatch with the exact saved value.

principle: NN/g Heuristic 2 (Match between system and real world)
screenshot: n/a (verified at 12:58 UTC during initial navigation)
problem: Navigating to /auth/signout directly (as a logged-in user might guess from old NextAuth conventions) returns a 404 'This page could not be found'. The correct sign-out flow is User → SIGN OUT button at bottom of /user page. The 404 is a leftover from a previous routing structure and breaks Jakob's Law expectations.
fix: Either (a) redirect /auth/signout to /user (with the sign-out card visible), or (b) implement /auth/signout as a confirmation page that posts to the real signout action. The 404 is the worst outcome.
